From childhood hardship in Indonesia to becoming a head chef in Dubai. 🇮🇩🇦🇪

Bobby Sutanto grew up in a family where every grain of rice mattered.

Nothing was wasted.

Every opportunity had to be earned.

Those early lessons in discipline, gratitude and resilience eventually took him from Indonesia to Singapore, Macau and finally Dubai in 2014.

Today, he leads multicultural kitchen teams at a renowned Dubai restaurant and works in one of the world’s most competitive culinary destinations.

But his success was not instant.

He had to adapt to new cultures, live far from family, manage pressure inside fast-paced kitchens and prove himself through consistency.

Dubai became the turning point that allowed him to:

Work with international chefs
Learn global hospitality standards
Lead diverse teams
Develop younger culinary talent
Build a career beyond what he once imagined

His biggest lesson?

Success is not only about reaching the top.
It is also about helping others reach the table.

Now, he wants to mentor young chefs and create opportunities for people who remind him of his younger self.

A powerful reminder for every UAE expat:

Your background does not decide your future.

Your discipline, gratitude and willingness to keep learning can change everything.

Save this story for the days you feel like giving up.
Share it with someone building a new life in the UAE.

What is the biggest lesson Dubai has taught you?
